## The Midpoint Rule

Approximate an integral by sampling the midpoint of each subinterval.

$$
M_n(f) = h \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f\left(a + \left(k+\frac{1}{2}\right)h\right),
\qquad h = \frac{b-a}{n}.
$$

This is the same example used in the Unbloated technical book.

## Reference Implementation

```python
def midpoint(f, a, b, n):
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError("n must be positive")
    h = (b - a) / n
    return h * sum(f(a + (k + 0.5) * h) for k in range(n))
```

## Checking the Result

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
For the integral of $x^2$ on $[0,1]$:

| $n$ | Estimate | Absolute error |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.250000 | 0.083333 |
| 2 | 0.312500 | 0.020833 |
| 4 | 0.328125 | 0.005208 |
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.callout-note}
These values check one integrand. They do not establish an error bound for
arbitrary continuous functions.
:::
